symptoms: Chest pain (made worse by coughing or deep breathing)
Dyspnea (shortness of breath, or difficult, labored breathing)
Orthopnea (the inability to breathe easily unless you're sitting up straight or standing up straight)
causes: Body producing too much fluid or not absorbing enough fluid
Transudative causes (increase in pressure from fluid): Heart failure, Cirrhosis, Nephrotic syndrome

Exudative causes (fluid getting through smallest blood vessels or lymphatic system not draining enough): Pneumonia, Cancer (lung cancer, breast cancer or lymphoma), Kidney disease, Inflammatory disease, Post open-heart surgery
Chylothorax (chyle from lymphatic system after trauma)
Meig's syndrome (from a benign ovarian tumor)
treatments: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) (with optional insertion of sterile talc or an antibiotic)
outlook: Varies depending on what caused it and what other conditions you have
For some people, treatment is successful, but effusions can happen again
Outlook isn't good when caused by cancer
complications: An infection that becomes an abscess
prevention: Sticking to low-salt meals if instructed
living_with: Stick to treatment plan for chronic condition
Go to all follow-up appointments to manage chronic condition
Get immediate help if having trouble breathing
